title: Generic isotopies have only Reidemeister singular times
statement: Let $F'$ be an isotopy in general position as in the preceding item, with exceptional times $t_1<\dots<t_N$, and for $t\notin\{t_1,\dots,t_N\}$ let $D_t$ be the regular projection of $F'_t$. Then: (a) for each $i$ and all sufficiently small $\delta>0$, the diagrams $D_{t_i-\delta}$ and $D_{t_i+\delta}$ are related by exactly one oriented Reidemeister move up to planar isotopy, of the following type: a vertical tangency of case (i) gives R1, a tangency of the slice with the double-point locus of case (ii) gives R2, and a transverse triple point of case (iii) gives R3; (b) for $t$ between consecutive exceptional times the diagrams are pairwise planar isotopic, and the movement from $t=0$ to $t=1$ is therefore a finite sequence of planar isotopies and Reidemeister moves taking the projection of $F'_0$ to that of $F'_1$; (c) the over/under and orientation data of each move are those carried by $F'$.
strategy: Local models with explicit Taylor expansions. (a) R1: if at $(u_0,t_0)$ the slice derivative vanishes, then in suitable coordinates $\pi\circ F'_{t_0+\delta}(u_0+\epsilon)\approx \mathrm{const}+(b\epsilon^2+d\delta,\, e\epsilon\delta+c\epsilon^3+d'\delta)$ with $b>0$, $e\neq0$, $c\neq0$; slices on the two sides differ by creating or deleting a kink, and the sign of the normal coordinate decides over/under: Queffelec section 3.3 (with Figure 6). (b) R2: at a time where the slice is tangent to the double-point locus, the two branches at the double point are, in suitable coordinates, two parabolas $(a_1\epsilon,b_1\epsilon^2)$, $(a_2\epsilon,b_2\epsilon^2)$ whose relative height is a nondegenerate linear function of $t$; on the two sides of the exceptional time they either miss or meet in two transverse crossings of opposite signs: Queffelec section 3.5 and Ozsvath-Stipsicz-Szabo Figure B.3. (c) R3: at a triple point the three branches have pairwise distinct directions and the moving branch crosses the intersection point of the other two; the two adjacent slices are related by R3, and the normal coordinates give the over/under pattern: Queffelec section 3.4. Completeness: a slice fails to be a diagram exactly when one of Conditions 1-3 fails, and those failures are exactly (i)-(iii), so no other local event occurs (Queffelec section 3.6). Authoring obligation: the source states (a) in detail and indicates (b), (c); the Step 3 author must write out the two indicated local computations, which are the displayed expansions above. The lemma is conditional on the general-position isotopy supplied by the preceding item and is itself choice-free: the local models use only the listed genericity properties, not the existence theorem that produced them.
